sections.html:
Voters approved incorporation on November 3, 2015, and Millcreek became a city on December 28, 2016. An earlier try in 2012 fell short with roughly 40 percent support. Before cityhood the area was Millcreek Township, which Salt Lake County created in 2002 so residents could steer local planning and avoid being absorbed by neighboring cities.

The first mayor and council took office in 2016, so city hall here is quite new. That matters little for a sale, except that some permit and zoning rules are only a few years old. Ask the city, not a neighbor, how a rule applies to your lot.

Most of the housing was built between the postwar years and the 1980s, when suburban building spread south from Salt Lake City. A house of that age usually gets its roof, plumbing and wiring checked first.

Millcreek lies between Salt Lake City and South Salt Lake to the north and Murray and Holladay to the south, at about 4,285 feet. Mill Creek Canyon rises directly to the east. Four community councils split the city.

  • Canyon Rim, in the northeast, has steeper ground.
  • East Mill Creek sits near the mouth of the canyon.
  • Mount Olympus takes in the Olympus Cove area in the eastern foothills.
  • The Millcreek area covers the western and central parts, which are the most densely developed.

Five ZIP codes touch the city: 84106, 84107, 84109, 84117 and 84124. A mailing address will not prove a house is inside Millcreek, so check the parcel record. Granite School District serves the whole city, and Skyline High School is its high school here.

sections.h2: Which parts of Millcreek carry earthquake, slope and flood rules?
sections.html:
Millcreek has a sensitive lands ordinance (case ZT-23-011) that covers fault lines and setbacks, liquefaction areas, steep slopes, the Mill Creek floodplain, avalanche and rockfall zones, alluvial fans, stream corridors, ridgelines and the wildland and urban interface. Mount Olympus debris flow areas roughly match slopes steeper than 30 percent.

Fault areas call for a fault survey, liquefaction areas for more soils study, and steep ground such as Canyon Rim for a slope analysis and a buildable area test.

  • These are building and addition rules, so they weigh most when a buyer plans to expand.
  • Call the city to find out whether a relief option for single-family homes applies to your lot.
  • An owner who disputes a hazard mapping can submit a site-specific geologic report to the county geologist.

sections.h2: Mill Creek Canyon and nearby homes
sections.html:
The canyon just east of the city is part of the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest and is undeveloped. It sits close to the East Mill Creek and Mount Olympus neighborhoods. Vehicles pay a $5 fee on the way out, an annual pass costs $50, and the upper half closes to vehicles from November 1 through July 1. Dogs may run off leash on trails only on odd-numbered days.

If your house sits near the canyon road, expect buyers to ask about weekend traffic and trail parking.

An ADU is allowed only on a lot with an owner-occupied home, and the city records a notice on the title to say so. Any title company will find that notice during a sale.

  • Internal and attached units can be short-term rentals with an ADU application and a Millcreek business license. Detached units cannot.
  • Rentals of 30 days or more are allowed in every ADU type with an ADU compliance letter and a business license.
  • Each unit needs at least one off-street parking stall, and a separate utility meter is not allowed.
  • A detached unit needs an R-1 or A zone, a lot of at least 8,000 square feet, up to 1,000 square feet of floor area and a rear-yard location.

Since everything hinges on owner occupancy, an investor who buys your house cannot count on keeping the ADU rentable. If you finished a basement apartment without a permit, say so early.

sections.h2: Primary residential exemption and the tax calendar
sections.html:
Utah taxes a primary home on 55 percent of its market value, while a second home is taxed on the full amount. To qualify, the state tax commission requires 183 consecutive days of use as a primary domicile in a calendar year, and a household can claim only one. A landlord renting to a full-time tenant can claim it too, by submitting a declaration signed by every owner.

The exemption does not move automatically to a new owner. A buyer who moves in files a fresh application with the county Board of Equalization by September 15, and a late one can cost that owner the exemption for the year. A 2026 change requires Form TC-473A starting January 1, 2027 whenever ownership changes, including deed or trust transfers.

On the county calendar, tax notices go out by November 1, payment is due without penalty on November 30, and delinquency starts December 1.

sections.h2: Selling a house with an unpermitted unit
sections.html:
A basement apartment without paperwork is the most common snag in this city. A conventional buyer's lender will want to know whether the unit is legal, and the answer depends on owner occupancy, the recorded notice and a compliance letter. If any of those are missing, the sale can stall in the middle of escrow.

Your options are to apply for the missing approvals before listing, to disclose the situation and price accordingly, or to sell as-is to a buyer who plans to sort it out. Tell the buyer what you know. Surprises found during inspection cost more than disclosures made up front.

After you accept a cash offer, the title company opens the file, searches the title and prepares the deed. You sign, the buyer funds, and the deed goes to the county for recording. Having the following on hand speeds things up: a photo ID, any estate or trust paperwork, and a mortgage payoff figure if you still owe on the house. Property tax for the year is generally divided between seller and buyer at closing.

sections.h2: What a Millcreek cash sale looks like
sections.html:
Selling for cash here removes the lender, the appraisal and the listing prep. You describe the house and we price it as it is. A title company then runs the signing and files the deed with the county.

Owners reach out when a house has an unpermitted unit, a hillside lot with a long repair list or a probate delay. Bring whatever you have on the unit, such as a compliance letter or the recorded notice, and we will factor it in. If the number does not work, you simply decline.

faqs.q: When did Millcreek become a city?
faqs.a: Millcreek incorporated on December 28, 2016, after a November 3, 2015 vote. It had been a county township since 2002.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Millcreek, Utah?
faqs.a: Granite School District serves the city, and Skyline High School is its high school here. Check the zone for your specific address.

faqs.q: Can I rent out an accessory dwelling unit in Millcreek?
faqs.a: Yes, if the lot has an owner-occupied home and the unit has a compliance letter. Internal and attached units can be short-term rentals with an ADU application and a city business license, but detached units cannot.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Millcreek?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes is $627,200. That is a citywide figure and does not predict what your house will bring.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Millcreek?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County sets November 30 as the last day to pay without penalty. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1.
